summary: @onereach/step-components preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style identifier renaming and, at install time, downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle whose contents are further obfuscated with a shuffled string-array + rotate-and-decode routine (`WV8StW`, `hc1jfK9`), making it opaque to Node-based inspection. The package advertises Vue step components; a Bun-compiled 727KB opaque bundle executed at preinstall has no relationship to that purpose. Fetching the Bun runtime from its official source is not itself the concern; the harm is that the runtime is used to execute an in-tarball, heavily-obfuscated, purpose-mismatched payload on every `npm install`, and the payload's behavior cannot be determined without full deobfuscation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
